messages:
emma: Heads-up — RiverBank POC starts Mon. They reported nondeterministic responses vs CompetitorX; goal is parity for the account-summary endpoint. Need a concrete plan: shim + prompt tests + pricing ask from procurement.

jake: On it. I'll run a quick diff on the top 500 prompts we have. Early guess: tokenization differences and temperature/defaults are the biggest sources, plus stop-seq handling.

li: Runtime note: their load profile is ~200 qps with 2–4 tokens/req avg. We'll likely need to reserve 2 Dedicated slots for steady throughput during the POC. Canary should be us-west1.

rajiv: Procurement wants a price mapping to CompetitorX. Can we quote equivalent per-100k requests and a bridging price? Also they asked about deterministic output options — what's the unit cost impact?

jake: Deterministic-ish = temp=0 / top_p=0. We don't expose RNG seeds. Deterministic configs can ↑repetition and may require more prompt engineering. Cost delta negligible per-token but may require more tokens for formatting.

sarah: Security questionnaire: they flagged encryption-at-rest + data residency. For the POC we can offer Private VPC in us-west1 and KMS integration. I'll prep SOC2 attestation, KMS onboarding notes, and a data-deletion SLA for review.

emma: Timeline proposal: 4-week POC. Week 1: compatibility shim + canonical prompt set. Week 2: run 5k prompts, gather diffs. Week 3: iterate prompts / add prompt templates. Week 4: production smoke + pricing negotiation.

jake: Suggest a small shim mapping CompetitorX payload -> Redwood chat/batch format. Example snippet to show them:
```json
// CompetitorX
{"prompt":"{{input}}","max_tokens":150,"temperature":0.7}
// Redwood
{"model":"redwood-2b","input":"{{input}}","max_output_tokens":150,"temperature":0.7}
```
Also call out response_meta differences: CompetitorX returns a single `completion` string while we return an `output` array with chunks/metadata. Shim should normalize to their shape.

li: Batching behavior differs — CompetitorX appears to do per-request batching client-side. Our runtime uses continuous batching which reduces cost but can add ~40–60ms latency depending on batch sizing. We can tune batch_size and max_wait_ms to match their latency SLO.

emma: Any enterprise blockers we should surface to the customer now?

sarah: Legal asked about data deletion SLA and retention for POC logs. We can offer a 30-day purge policy for POC data (subject to legal sign-off). Also need to confirm whether they require pseudonymization or extra audit fields.

rajiv: For pricing I'll propose a bridge rate: match CompetitorX's effective per-request $0.0015 for first 1M calls to remove friction, then our standard tiering with options for Dedicated flat fee. Add an optional engineering support retainer for any parity work.

jake: For parity measurement, propose metrics: token-level diff rate, semantic similarity using embeddings (cosine < 0.92 flagged), and a manual pass rate for top 200 business-critical prompts. Also track normalized output length and stop-token differences.

emma: Can someone assemble the prompt-set and send to RiverBank by EOD Friday?

jake: I'll export 500 anonymized prompts from our sandbox and convert to their schema. Any constraints on PII in those prompts?

sarah: Redact PII — mask emails, SSNs, and run the set through our DLP. I'll coordinate with eng-sre for automated redaction.

li: infra-bot shows capacity: us-west1 spare GPUs: 6, but two already earmarked. I'll reserve 2 and submit allocation ticket.
infra-bot: reservation request #TCK-482 submitted.

rajiv: Quick sales question — what if they demand exact token-level parity with CompetitorX?

jake: Exact token parity is basically impossible when models differ. Recommend a "behavioral parity" SLA: pass >=95% of test prompts under our similarity metrics + manual review for failures. Flag the truly blocking cases (legal/regulatory outputs) for special handling.

emma: OK — finalize a short runbook. I'll create a shared doc and assign owners. Quick checklist here: shim, prompt set, security docs, pricing bridge, Dedicated reservation, canary plan, demo script.

sarah: I'll attach SOC2 cert and KMS onboarding doc to the runbook and handle the questionnaire answers. Noting: RiverBank is not requesting HIPAA controls, but we should keep the packet ready.

jake: One more technical: stop-sequence behavior — CompetitorX implicitly strips trailing newlines and trims punctuation; our outputs preserve trailing whitespace. Normalize in shim: trim trailing whitespace, canonicalize punctuation to reduce spurious diffs.

emma: Great. Meeting with RiverBank Tue 10am — prep deck + short demo. Who can join?

rajiv: I'll lead pricing & procurement.
jake: I'll run the parity demo and bring the diff dashboard.
sarah: I'll be on the security Qs.
li: I'll standby for infra/canary questions.

emma: Perfect — I'll post the runbook link after lunch and ping calendar invites. :rocket:
